snippet.title: Without a Doubt | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
In May of 2026, Braydon Bringhurst stood at the bottom of Gouranga, an iconic double-black-diamond descent in Squamish, British Columbia. The trail is steep, technical and high consequence, and will give even experienced riders jitters. 

But Braydon wasn’t there just to ride down Gouranga. He’d done that already, many times. This time, he was there to ride up it. 

Impossible? Likely. But that uncertainty is where Braydon thrives, and each failure is just another piece of the larger process. And for Braydon, that’s where the joy lies.

snippet.title: Running with Huemuls
snippet.description:
Fundo Puchegüín is a newly protected area within the Cochamó commune. It connects one of the largest biological corridors in Latin America—a key bridge for species like the huemul to roam freely and recover their habitat. 

For Patagonia ambassador Felipe Cancino, seeing a huemul in the wild “is like seeing a ghost.” The southernmost deer in the world, this shy inhabitant of Patagonia is a national icon on Chile’s coat of arms. It’s also critically endangered. So when researchers confirmed a previously undocumented population of huemul in Fundo Puchegüín, he saw an opportunity. 

Along with fellow Patagonia ambassador and climate scientist Peyton Thomas, Felipe covered 75 miles through native forest, on seldom-traveled trails, searching for signs that the ghost of Patagonia had passed through this land.

snippet.title: Without a Doubt: Inside the Mind of Braydon Bringhurst | Trailer | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
“I fail all the time. I would say I’m a professional failer.” – Braydon Bringhurst

In May of 2026, Braydon stood at the bottom of Gouranga, a double-black-diamond descent in Squamish, British Columbia. But Braydon wasn’t there just to ride down Gouranga. He was there to try and ride up it.

“Without a Doubt: Inside the Mind of Braydon Bringhurst” documents Braydon’s attempt to ride up Gouranga and how he finds joy in the process…even when that process involves a whole lot of failure.

Stay tuned…full film dropping soon.

snippet.title: Meet Austin
snippet.description:
Austin’s passion for fishing began on his family’s farm in Atchison, Kansas, where he learned to pursue warmwater species before later discovering fly fishing on the freestone and tailwater rivers of Colorado. Fly fishing has been a constant in his life ever since, and a way to share the outdoors and build connections through time spent on the water. 

While attending Penn State University as a track athlete in high jump (his personal best was nearly 6´11˝), Austin spent much of his free time fly fishing throughout the Appalachians, further developing his skills and love for wild fish. Today, Austin is a fly fishing guide in Colorado, as well as the founder and executive director of Community Fly Fishing, a nonprofit that offers free 101 sessions, guided instructional outings, river conservation efforts, and guide and instructor courses. 

“The rhythm of the river and tide grounds me in a connection to nature like nothing else,” he says, “and I’m grateful to be able to live a life with a rod in my hand.” 

Welcome to the team, Austin.

snippet.title: Meet Austin
snippet.description:
Fly fishing asks something of you before it gives anything back.

You have to be present. You have to be still. You have to watch the water, listen to it and earn the drift. Austin Campbell learned that on his family's farm in Atchison, Kansas - chasing warmwater species long before he ever found his way to the freestone and tailwater rivers of Colorado. Once he did, fly fishing never let go.

Today Austin guides on those same Colorado rivers and runs Community Fly Fishing - a nonprofit he founded to lower the barrier of entry to a sport that has long belonged to a narrow slice of people. Free 101 sessions. Guided instructional outings. River conservation. A door held open for anyone who wants to walk through it.

Because for Austin it has never been about the number of fish. It's about the process - and making sure more people get to be part of it.

"The rhythm of the river and tide grounds me in a connection to nature like nothing else," he says. "And I'm grateful to be able to live a life with a rod in my hand."

Welcome to the team, Austin.

snippet.title: Without a Doubt Trailer | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
In May of 2026, Braydon Bringhurst stood at the bottom of Gouranga, an iconic double-black-diamond descent in Squamish, British Columbia. The trail is steep, technical and high consequence, and will give even experienced riders jitters. 

But Braydon wasn’t there just to ride down Gouranga. He’d done that already, many times. This time, he was there to ride up it. 

Impossible? Likely. But that uncertainty is where Braydon thrives, and each failure is just another piece of the larger process. And for Braydon, that’s where the joy lies.

In May of 2026, Braydon Bringhurst stood at the bottom of Gouranga, an iconic double-black-diamond descent in Squamish, British Columbia. The trail is steep, technical and high consequence, and will give even experienced riders jitters. 

But Braydon wasn’t there just to ride down Gouranga. He’d done that already, many times. This time, he was there to ride up it. 

Impossible? Likely. But that uncertainty is where Braydon thrives, and each failure is just another piece of the larger process. And for Braydon, that’s where the joy lies.

snippet.title: Meet Canyon
snippet.description:
Canyon Woodward is one of the strongest emerging trail runners in the US, shaped by years of big-effort running in his home range of the Smoky Mountains. He's taken that foundation to both racing and personal mountain objectives, earning major wins nationwide and back-to-back top-three American finishes at UTMB. He also holds the FKT on the notoriously demanding S.C.A.R. route in the Smokies, and now has his sights set on a highly anticipated Western States 100 debut at the end of June. 

Off the trail, Canyon brings a deep commitment to community and environmental work. He cofounded Dirtroad Organizing, a nonprofit focused on empowering the next generation of progressive rural organizers, and his writing has appeared in some of the country's most celebrated publications. 

"Trail running fascinates me as a means to explore landscapes," he says. "Physical ones, of course, but more so those that defy articulation: of the mind and body, of relationships and of community.” We're excited to do some exploring with you, Canyon.

Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: Ever think about your jacket’s journey? What would it say if it could talk?
snippet.description:
Trade in your Patagonia gear: https://pat.ag/YTS/IfThisJacketCouldTalk

A jacket can carry more than a little dust. It can carry the memory of every peak, road trip and adventure along the way. So, what would yours say if it could talk?

After years of bagging peaks, riding in the back of a Subaru and collecting a little dust along the way, one Patagonia jacket finds itself on a counter for inspection. Still good, they say. A quick clean-up later, it is back out there with a new owner, ready for whatever comes next-and possibly ready to outlast them, too.

Patagonia Trade-In helps eligible used gear continue its story. Clothing and packs that are still functional and in good condition can be traded in for credit toward new or used purchases in stores or online-because a jacket with more life in it should not be done yet. Sometimes, the gear that has already been places is exactly the gear ready to go somewhere new.

Keep a good story going.

Created by Donnie Hedden and Ian McMullen

snippet.title: Meet Braydon
snippet.description:
Braydon Bringhurst puts the “down” in “up” … or maybe it’s the “up” in “down”. The Boise-based rider’s explosive style defies directions and disciplines,  and he’s as smooth boosting off natural rock features as he is hopping up them. The father of three is also incredibly kind and humble, a perfect combo for coaching local kids, hosting events like the Boise Mountain Bike Festival and running his Hard MTB League.  

Making it look so easy, however, takes a lot of hard work. Braydon’s dedication is superhuman (his background includes national victories in BMX racing, a national championship for freeskiing, an All-American status in collegiate pole vault and an MBA degree), and he puts in countless hours of mental and physical training long before he ever rides a line.   

“This stuff I’m doing might look crazy, but in my head it’s nothing more than another step of my progression, and that progression comes from a ton of work and a ton of deliberate effort and practice. By the time I’m doing it, there are no question marks in my mind. There’s no fear. I’m just executing.” 

Hyped to get out for a rip, Braydon. Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: Meet Babsi
snippet.description:
Babsi Vigl has always been fascinated by climbing; it’s also always been about more than summiting (though she has bagged plenty of those, too). Raised in the Austrian Alps, she’s been climbing since she was a child and went on her first expedition at the age of 20. In the years since, she has explored the Himalaya, Patagonia, Yosemite, Alaska and countless other ranges around the world. 

As impressive as her long list of objectives, however, are all her other roles in the climbing community: She’s also an occupational therapist who specializes in healing injured climbers; an instructor who teaches young mountaineers and mentors women in the alpine, and a professional writer who captures stories that make up the sport she loves. 

“I think I’m a really curious person, and I feel there’s still so much to discover in my sport,” she says. “Even a route you’ve climbed 100 times, you can go back and find something new: it’s a different season, or you have new skills. Our planet is really big and there are so many places and communities to discover. Too many for one life.” 

Excited to do some exploring with you, Babsi. Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: This Is Not a Drill | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
As extreme weather around the world grows deadlier, a new generation of leaders is rising to face the challenges. 
From Oscar®-nominated filmmakers, director Oren Jacoby and writer-producer Betsy West, This Is Not a Drill documents three unlikely heroes as they take on one of the most powerful industries in the world. 
Twenty-five-year-old Justin J. Pearson rallies a multiracial grassroots coalition to try and defeat a crude oil pipeline in Memphis, Tennessee. Roishetta Ozane, a mother of six from Louisiana, transforms personal loss into political action, taking her fight from the storm-ravaged streets to the halls of Congress. Sharon Wilson, a former oil insider turned methane hunter, uses infrared cameras to expose invisible, deadly gases pouring from fracking sites and pipelines in Texas that have been hiding in plain sight. Backing them are unlikely allies, descendants of John D. Rockefeller, who are exposing ExxonMobil’s decades-long cover up. Together, this coalition uncovers what they call Big Oil’s “Big Con” - an industry doubling down on fossil fuels while disguising the truth.

THIS IS NOT A DRILL, which premiered at the Telluride Film Festival, is the story of courage, betrayal and grassroots victories showing how people, armed with only grit and determination, can stand up to power.

snippet.title: Free Climbing Madagascar’s King Line | Field Report | Patagonia
snippet.description:
Patagonia Ambassador Dörte Pietron and her partner, Daniel Gebel, found some of the best climbing but worst protection in Madagascar. After getting skunked on multiple routes due to corroded bolts or terrible bolt lines, they fell in love with Lalan'i Mpanjaka (8a+/5.13c). Malagasy for “the King Line,” the pair pulled out every trick in the book to give themselves the best chance of success on the sharp granite and impeccable movement of this  11-pitch, 1,968-foot beauty.

snippet.title: Meet Cash
snippet.description:
Cash is what happens when you give a surfboard wings. Born and raised on Maui, the young waterman has been surfing his entire life and picked up foiling in his mid-teens. Cash surfs when the waves are clean and the wind is down; when they’re not, his foil turns bumps and chop into a magic carpet ride, allowing him to stay out on the water longer with his friends, be it in the ocean or on a lake or river. As he puts it, “a one-foot wave on a foil can feel like a six-foot wave on a surfboard.” 
 
Despite just turning 20 years old, Cash is already pushing the boundaries of what’s possible on a foil with a unique style that’s as playful as it is cutting edge, so much so that he has a signature technique, the Berzolla Bottom Turn. Whatever he’s riding, Cash is just happy to be on the water. 

“Being on land can be so crazy and can make life feel super intense,” he says. “But when I hop in the water, I’m focused on one thing and one thing only. It brings me a peace of mind, helps me relax and most importantly, it’s fun.” 

Hyped to catch some waves with you, Cash. Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: Oly Ties His Mug Bug | Oly’s Dean | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
The "Mug Bug," demonstrated by its creator, 9-year-old Oly Hickman, is designed to fool wild steelhead on British Columbia’s Dean River. Not much to it—a size-2 hook, some grizzly hackle and moose hair. Just a good idea that does what it’s supposed to do. 

In the film “Oly’s Dean,” we follow Oly as he explores life along one of the planet’s most productive steelhead rivers, where curiosity and chasing toads matter just as much as catching steelhead.

snippet.title: This is Not a Drill Trailer | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
Watch the full film here: https://youtu.be/kjcR-pAjBiw

As extreme weather around the world grows deadlier, a new generation of leaders is rising to
face the challenges. 

From Oscar®-nominated filmmakers, director Oren Jacoby and writer-producer Betsy West, This Is Not a Drill documents three unlikely heroes as they take on one of the most powerful industries in the world. 

Twenty-five-year-old Justin J. Pearson rallies a multiracial grassroots coalition to try and defeat a crude oil pipeline in Memphis, Tennessee. Roishetta Ozane, a mother of six from Louisiana, transforms personal loss into political action, taking her fight from the storm-ravaged streets to the halls of Congress. Sharon Wilson, a former oil insider turned methane hunter, uses infrared cameras to expose invisible, deadly gases pouring from fracking sites and pipelines in Texas that have been hiding in plain sight. Backing them are unlikely allies, descendants of John D. Rockefeller, who are exposing ExxonMobil’s decades-long cover up. Together, this coalition uncovers what they call Big Oil’s “Big Con” - an industry doubling down on fossil fuels while disguising the truth.

THIS IS NOT A DRILL, which premiered at the Telluride Film Festival, is the story of courage, betrayal and grassroots victories showing how people, armed with only grit and determination, can stand up to power.

snippet.title: The Free Wall Kit | Lor Sabourin on Daedalus
snippet.description:
When Patagonia Ambassador Lor Sabourin got out to the “desert alpine” of northern Arizona to get on two modern classics, Dickel’s Delight (5.13c) and Daedalus (5.13+), they knew they would need all their best tactics for working difficult multipitch projects. That included both hard tactics, like hauling up a bag or toprope soloing crux moves, and soft tactics, like taking care of their mental capacity and staying tapped into their gratitude for being out there.

snippet.title: Oly’s Dean | A Kid, a River and a Different Way of Growing Up
snippet.description:
Set along British Columbia’s remote Dean River, “Oly’s Dean” follows 9-year-old Oly Hickman as he moves through his family’s fishing lodge in the heart of steelhead country.

Each summer, anglers from around the world come to swing flies for the Dean’s legendary fish. Bears roam the shoreline. The river runs cold and clear. Oly, however, is just as content chasing toads as wild steelhead.

More interested in wanderings than trophies, he explores the wilderness on his own terms. At an age when his father, veteran guide Jeff Hickman, can turn him loose and trust him to be safe, Oly ties flies of his own design and learns the rhythms of lodge life in a place that rewards curiosity.

When he hooks and lands a chrome-bright wild steelhead on a fly he created himself, the moment feels less like conquest than connection. Through quiet observation, “Oly’s Dean” captures a childhood rooted in independence and stewardship—and parents learning to see the world with a renewed sense of wonder.

snippet.title: Meet Jenny
snippet.description:
Jenny’s path to mountain exploration started in the North Cascades, backpacking with her family. She caught the rock-climbing bug in her mid-20s, lived in a van and traveled with the conditions, ticking off well-respected alpine routes in Canada, Patagonia and Europe. During COVID, Jenny discovered a penchant for running and took it into the mountains, rediscovering areas she’d often been with a heavy climbing kit. She loved how much faster she could go with just a lightweight pack. Jenny started expanding the traditional definition of trail running, mixing technical rock skills with the simplicity of running. Her favorite form of mountain expression involves long, complex routes that mix trail and off-trail travel, just seeing how far and she can get.   

“It doesn’t matter whether you call it trail running, or mountain running or ultra-neering,” she says. “Moving through the mountains unencumbered by a heavy load is a special form of freedom.”  

Excited to do some exploring with you, Jenny. Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: Meet Jack
snippet.description:
For a 21-year-old, Jack Ho has had a hell of a career. Born and raised on O‘ahu, Hawai‘i, right next to the world-famous beaches of Waikiki, Jack started surfing when he was 5 years old and he hasn’t left the water since. That passion only intensified when, at age 13, his dad bought him a foil, which he pursued with a dedication that would quickly make him one of the best in the world. Two years later, he and a group of friends discovered downwinders, and the “Voyager Foilers” have spent the past half-decade pushing the limits of what’s possible on a foil … though Jack can still be found off the shore of O‘ahu paddling his short and longboards to catch the next swell. 

“My love for surfing started at a young age, and no matter what I do, I can’t shake it off,” he says. “It’s a passion that sticks with me, and the root of it is riding waves every type of way, getting out there and enjoying what my home has to offer. That’s so valuable to me and something I take a lot of pride in.” 

So hyped to get on the water with you, Jack. Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: Meet Lucas
snippet.description:
Lucas Wachs is a snowboarder’s skier; he never misses a side hit and rarely goes in a straight line. Having grown up on the natural terrain park of Mt. Bachelor riding with mostly snowboarders, the Bend, Oregon, local was destined to be unconventional: his slashy, surfy style turns any slope into a playground, with a versatility that defies labels or disciplines. Lucas brings that mindset to everything he rides, from PNW pillows to Alaskan spines to touring up one of Oregon’s volcanoes, and he’s more interested than ever to explore where the skintrack can take him. 
 
He’s also a badass mountain biker, skateboarder, snowboarder and surfer, skills that continue to influence his skiing. Whatever Lucas is doing, you can guarantee two things: He’ll do it his own way, and he’ll do it with style. 
 
“As a skier, I think I look at the mountains in different ways,” he says. “I learned a lot from snowboarders growing up and how they approach terrain, and I think that set me apart from other people. Not better; just a different take.” 

 
So stoked to send it with you, Lucas. Welcome to the team. 

About Patagonia (for the SEO)
Patagonia was founded on a simple idea: build the best gear while protecting the places we love. Our commitment to the planet shows up in everything we make, using recycled materials and transparent supply chains alongside Worn Wear repairs that keep gear in action longer. When you're chasing storms, climbing peaks, or just exploring close to home, our gear moves with you and helps protect the wild for future generations.

Learn more about Patagonia: https://pat.ag/Patagonia

snippet.title: Meet Austen
snippet.description:
Austen “the Froth Goblin” Sweetin is Pacific Northwest, through and through. Born in Seattle, Washington, he’s been shaped by both the area’s deep snowboarding culture and steep, technical terrain since his earliest years, a background that’s made him one of the sport’s most versatile and exciting riders. He can power down Alaskan spines as smoothly as he can 10-story pillow stacks, all while spinning and tricking off every feature like a cat on a bender. Now Austen is taking those freeride skills to the skintrack, using human power to find new lines and chase after bigger objectives. 
 
“The thing that really keeps me getting after it is the ceiling, the unknown,” he says. “What’s the next forecast going to look like? What’s this mountain range going to be like? It’s that constant evolution, that newness, that keeps me pursuing at a deeper level.” 
That passion and energy have made him one of snowboarding’s most beloved figures, and whether you’re watching him surf, skate or pick riffs on his guitar, Austen makes you want to go snowboarding. 
 
Hyped to have you, Froth Goblin. Welcome to the team.

snippet.title: Field Report | Baffin Island with Céline Jaccard, Pachi Ibarra, Violeta Sepúlveda
snippet.description:
In one of the most remote regions on the planet, Chilean climbers Pachi Ibarra and Violeta Sepúlveda, together with Swiss-Canadian Céline Jaccard, face the climate and uncertainty of the Arctic during a self-supported expedition on Baffin Island. After spending more than twenty days as guests of the mountains there, the three women put up the first ascent of Mini Asgard with their new route La Casa de las Diosas (5.12?, C1, 220m) with perseverance, respect and humor. 

Chapters:
0:00 Arctic Wilderness of Baffin Island
0:38 Planning the Expedition
1:28 Discovering Mini Asgard
2:47 At the Base of the Climb
3:04 First Attempt on the North Face
4:12 Storm and Changing Conditions
6:01 Back on the Wall
7:02 Summit of Mini Asgard

About Patagonia:
Patagonia was founded on a simple idea: build the best gear while protecting the places we love. Our commitment to the planet shows up in everything we make, using recycled materials and transparent supply chains alongside Worn Wear repairs that keep gear in play longer. When you're chasing storms, climbing peaks, or just exploring close to home, our gear moves with you and helps protect the wild for future generations.

snippet.title: Offseason: Marie-France Roy | Patagonia
snippet.description:
Marie-France Roy’s world is shaped by connection, from snow-covered mountains to the kelp forests of the Pacific Ocean.

A Patagonia Snow ambassador based on the coast of British Columbia, Marie spends her winters riding big mountain lines. But in the offseason, her focus shifts downstream, quite literally, toward the ocean and the ecosystems that depend on it.

Patagonia Snowboard ambassador Marie-France Roy’s world is connected by snow up high and kelp down low. When she’s not riding big mountains, she’s working to help the kelp forests off British Columbia thrive.

Drawn to the wildness of the coast, Marie has developed a deep connection to kelp, a fast-growing marine plant that supports biodiversity, captures carbon and plays a critical role in ocean health. Through drone mapping and collaboration with local conservation groups, she’s helping monitor kelp beds and better understand how they’re changing over time.

For Marie, everything is connected. Snow falling high in the mountains eventually makes its way to the ocean, linking environments that might seem far apart. That perspective shapes how she moves through both, whether on a snowboard or in the water.

Watch our “Offseason” series to learn more about what our ambassadors are up to when the wetsuits, waders and bibs come off.

When you're chasing storms, climbing peaks, or just exploring close to home, our gear moves with you and helps protect the wild for future generations.

snippet.title: Stories We Wear: Bryden Bowley | Patagonia
snippet.description:
In rural Pennsylvania, along the banks of the Allegheny River, snowboard filmmaker Bryden Bowley has quietly built a collection of used Patagonia gear that spans 50 years. For Bryden, capturing moments of his friends on snow and collecting vintage clothing remind him of the value of preservation. And making new memories in secondhand gear helps him stay in the present, “when the most meaningful things can happen.” 

Watch the short film to learn how his obsession, snowboarding and a love of the natural world led him to see ownership as an antidote to overconsumption.

00:00 A Small-Town Welcome 
01:11 A Family of Thrifters: Where It Started
01:27 Growing Up in Rural Pennsylvania
01:54 The Patagonia Collector Community 
02:12 A Yard-Sale Find: The Chouinard Carabiner
02:25 The Color That Keeps Coming Back in Outdoor Gear
02:57 Retro Rhythm Hoody
03:50 Travel Memories 
04:07 Snowboard Filmmaking: Risk, Trust, and What Gear Represents
04:50 Vintage Collecting: Preserving Stories, Rethinking Consumption

About Patagonia:
Patagonia was founded on a simple idea: build the best gear while protecting the places we love. Our commitment to the planet shows up in everything we make, using recycled materials and transparent supply chains alongside Worn Wear repairs that keep gear in action longer. When you're chasing storms, climbing peaks, or just exploring close to home, our gear moves with you and helps protect the wild for future generations.

localized.title: Stories We Wear: Bryden Bowley | Patagonia
localized.description:
In rural Pennsylvania, along the banks of the Allegheny River, snowboard filmmaker Bryden Bowley has quietly built a collection of used Patagonia gear that spans 50 years. For Bryden, capturing moments of his friends on snow and collecting vintage clothing remind him of the value of preservation. And making new memories in secondhand gear helps him stay in the present, “when the most meaningful things can happen.” 

Watch the short film to learn how his obsession, snowboarding and a love of the natural world led him to see ownership as an antidote to overconsumption.

snippet.title: Simple As A Turn | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
For Nicholas Wolken, turning is more than snowboarding’s foundation. It’s the simplest expression of what riding is all about. And from going pro to shaping snowboards made for turns, he’s spent much of his life chasing the deep feelings that come with carving on snow. Sure, the act of turning might be simple. But when mind, body, and board collide in a perfect toeside, simple has never felt more supernatural.

Patagonia Films presents
A Yucca Films production

snippet.title: Behind the Climb: Colin Haley & Tyler Karow on the Southeast Ridge of Cerro Torre | Patagonia
snippet.description:
In December 2024, Patagonia Ambassadors Colin Haley and Tyler Karow joined forces to climb the Southeast Ridge (Filo Sureste) of Cerro Torre in Patagonia. Considered the modern hard classic of Chaltén, Colin had made three previously unsuccessful attempts on the route before taking it on with Tyler. With a great weather window, impeccable bivies, highly efficient teamwork and optimal Beethoven listening, the two made this ascent a dream come true.

snippet.title: Cochamó por siempre | Una victoria de conservación que nace desde la comunidad
snippet.description:
¡Victoria en Chile! La compra exitosa del Fundo Puchegüín, liderada por Conserva Puchegüín, proyecta un nuevo futuro para la conservación y establece un gran logro para nuestro hogar, el planeta Tierra.  

En diciembre pasado, Conserva Puchegüín -una coalición de organizaciones dedicadas a la conservación, científicos y miembros de la comunidad local- concretó la compra de un territorio de alto valor ecológico conocido como el Fundo Puchegüín. Con el apoyo de Holdfast Collective, la organización sin fines de lucro de Patagonia, esta adquisición protege para siempre su biodiversidad, las costumbres y modos de vida de sus habitantes, así como su valor como espacio para las actividades y deportes al aire libre, tanto en el valle de Cochamó como en sus alrededores.  

Lo que sigue ahora es el desarrollo de un nuevo modelo de conservación, liderado y cocreado por personas que aman, defienden y habitan este territorio, que marca un hito para nuestro planeta.

snippet.title: How a Remote Valley in Chile Was Protected for the Future: Cochamó Forever! | Patagonia
snippet.description:
Tucked deep in southern Chile, Cochamó Valley has long felt untouched - no roads cutting through it, no engines overhead, just rainforest, granite walls and the people who call it home. When the land was put up for sale, the future of this place hung in the balance. What followed wasn’t a takeover by developers or investors, but something far rarer: a community stepping forward to protect what they love.

At its heart are the local residents, climbers, conservationists and neighbors who came together to secure Fundo Puchegüín and ensure its protection far into the future. Their work connects millions of acres of protected land across Chile and Argentina and introduces a new model of conservation - one led by the people who live on the land, shaped by shared responsibility, and grounded in care for future generations.

Cochamó’s story is proof that protecting wild places doesn’t have to mean excluding people. Sometimes it means trusting them.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: The Selkirk Shwack: bushwhacking, alpine running and glacier travel across BC's Selkirks | Patagonia
snippet.description:
“The Selkirk Shwack” began as an idea sketched out on a map: roughly 50 miles of dense bushwhacking, alpine running and glacier travel across British Columbia’s Selkirk Mountains, connecting the “big bend” of the Columbia River from west to east. Watch the Patagonia Story to see every challenge they faced.

In the summer of 2024, Matthew Tufts enlisted two equally curious friends who were game to find out. They would travel light, with running gear, harnesses, tag lines and a minimalist overnight kit. In the end, they learned much more about embracing “success” as a relative term—even in the face of failure.  

Read the story here: https://pat.ag/YT/SelkirkSchwack

Watch more Patagonia Stories: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aD57zBD1K4o&list=PLJQsrK_W2jni180Hq32OQRAjxSU3lltNI

snippet.title: Swiftcurrent Waders | Innovation Built on Exploration
snippet.description:
More than five decades of outdoor leadership have taught us a few things about building waders: the value of reliability, the advantages of intuitive design and the importance of accountability to our customers and our planet. We are never finished learning, questioning, tinkering and improving.
 
To bring our 2025 Swiftcurrent Waders to life, we listened to customer feedback, analyzed dozens of new fabrics, auditioned different material combinations and evaluated countless fit, design and feature tweaks. Our team of hardcore field testers punished prototype after prototype for more than three years of on-the-water testing and refinement.
 
Built with innovative materials, intuitive features and a refined fit, our Swiftcurrent® Waders are a better wader experience. Repatterned for bulk reduction, reduced seam stress, increased maneuverability and improved repairability, they move better in and out of the water, carry gear more efficiently and keep tools handy. They adjust to temperature changes better and switch from chest-high to waist-high quickly. They’re made from recycled materials without intentionally added “forever chemicals” known as PFAS. We even pattern them so they’re easier to put on, take off, and repair.
 
Motivated by relentless curiosity and a passion for the wild fish and clean waters we love, Patagonia Fly Fishing is thrilled to present the 2025 Swiftcurrent Wader Line.
 
2025 Swiftcurrent Waders:
Men’s Swiftcurrent® Expedition Zip-Front Waders
Women’s Swiftcurrent® Expedition Zip-Front Waders

snippet.description:

Since 2015, the group has brought solar to 123 homes. Learn more about Native Renewables and other environmental groups we support at https://pat.ag/YT/NativeRenewables.

snippet.title: PowSlayer Freeride Kit: Built for Hunting the Steepest and Deepest Powder | Patagonia
snippet.description:
It’s a bold goal to make the best better. Over the past 12 years, our PowSlayer Series has earned a near mythical status among those seeking the steepest, deepest powder in the biggest mountains. These aren't the ones bragging at the end of the day; they are the ones who let their tracks do the talking, who start before sunrise and leave behind lines as proud as they are nameless. Our new PowSlayer Freeride Kit is built for those riders.

Each piece of the PowSlayer Freeride Kit has been designed, patterned and tested together to ensure they all interact seamlessly, allowing us to align every pocket, cuff, hood and feature in a way that supports mobility, easy adjustments and unfettered accessibility. Start your day with the kit designed for skintrack including Nano-Air Ultralight Freeride Jacket and PowSlayer snow pants. Transition with the PowSlayer backpack and DAS Light Shorts, Skirt, and Hoody. Enjoy the descent with the PowSlayer Jacket and Pants.

snippet.title: Why Southern Forests Are Disappearing 4x Faster Than the Amazon
snippet.description:
To celebrate 40+ years of environmental grantmaking at Patagonia, we’re sharing brand-new stories from longtime partners like the Dogwood Alliance, which mobilizes people to protect forests and communities from industrial logging in the Southern US.   

“Trees are the solution for pollution. But when you start cutting those trees up, turning them into pellets and then burning them for energy, it creates a major human problem,” says Treva Gear, the Georgia campaign manager for Dogwood Alliance.  

More than a million acres of US forests have already been cut for biomass, directly exposing frontline communities to heavy pollution. Leaders like Treva are part of a growing movement to stop even more destruction in forests and communities across the South. 

“We’re going to fight and push back against this industry to protect our trees, to protect our health, to protect our planet.”  

Learn more about Dogwood Alliance at https://pat.ag/YT/Dogwood.

snippet.title: Cold-Water Wetsuit Testing in British Columbia
snippet.description:
In remote British Columbia, wetsuits, hoods, gloves and booties are not optional. They found waves, shrimp, fish, a wealth of tree-laden backdrops and a delightful shortage of cell reception.

snippet.title: These Activists Track Wolverines and the Impact of Climate Change
snippet.description:
To celebrate 40+ years of environmental grantmaking at Patagonia, we’re sharing brand-new stories from our longtime nonprofit partners like the Cascades Wolverine Project, which blends science, storytelling and recreation to support wolverine recovery for the benefit of people and wildlife. 

Rain or shine, the team skis out to remote wolverine habitat sites across the Pacific Northwest to set up cameras, monitors the sites throughout the seasons and then shares the data they collect to advance further research and community science efforts.

“Wolverines depend on deep snow in order to survive,” says Stephanie Williams, the group’s cofounder. “Tracking whether or not they can adapt to this changing climate means that we’re also in some ways tracking our own fate.” 

Learn more about Cascades Wolverine Project at https://pat.ag/YT/Cascades.

snippet.title: These Activists Track Wolverines and the Impact of Climate Change
snippet.description:
To celebrate 40+ years of environmental grantmaking at Patagonia, we’re sharing brand-new stories from our longtime nonprofit partners like the Cascades Wolverine Project, which blends science, storytelling and recreation to support wolverine recovery for the benefit of people and wildlife. 

Rain or shine, the team skis out to remote wolverine habitat sites across the Pacific Northwest to set up cameras, monitors the sites throughout the seasons and then shares the data they collect to advance further research and community science efforts.

“Wolverines depend on deep snow in order to survive,” says Stephanie Williams, the group’s cofounder. “Tracking whether or not they can adapt to this changing climate means that we’re also in some ways tracking our own fate.” 

Learn more about Cascades Wolverine Project at https://pat.ag/YT/Cascades.

snippet.title: Pheasant Tail Bonefish by Yvon Chouinard | Fly Recipe
snippet.description:
The general rule of matching fly color to bottom color doesn’t apply to pheasant tail flies—they work equally well over light sand or dark bottoms. What matters is having different sizes and weights. Jig hooks provide good action and ride hook-point up to avoid bottom snags.

MATERIALS
Hook: Umpqua U560BL-BN, #8–#12; Umpqua U555 Jig, #8–#12
Thread: 6/0 UNI-Thread, black or olive
Eyes: Dazl-Eyes, nontoxic
Ribbing: Medium copper wire
Tails: 8–10 pheasant tail barbs
Body: Pheasant tail barbs used for tails
Thorax: Hareline Hare’e Ice Dub, peacock
Hackle: Hungarian partridge, brown back feather

snippet.title: Pheasant Tail Foam Beetle by Craig Mathews | Fly Recipe
snippet.description:
Big trout can be counted on to investigate the distinctive plop an insect makes when clumsily falling into the water. Large beetles bumble along shorelines and often tumble in, while others crash-land when they mistake the water’s surface for solid ground. Either way, a big trout’s take is often heard rather than seen when the fish noisily slurps in this beetle pattern.

MATERIALS
Hook: Tiemco TMC 100BL, #8–#16
Thread: 6/0 or 8/0 UNI-Thread, black
Shellback: Black closed-cell foam, 2 mm
Body: 6–10 pheasant tail barbs
Legs: Fine rubber legs
Indicator: Brightly colored closed-cell foam
Head: Trimmed butt of shellback foam

snippet.title: Pheasant Tail Iris Caddis by Craig Mathews | Fly Recipe
snippet.description:
Because most caddis emerge and leave the water quickly, trout often favor struggling insects that are going nowhere—trapped in their pupal shucks with body and wings stuck. The natural texture of pheasant tail barbs traps air bubbles and sparkles, closely imitating an emerging caddis. The pattern floats high, and the visible wing makes it easier to track in late-evening light.

MATERIALS
Hook: Tiemco TMC 102Y, #15–#19
Thread: 8/0 UNI-Thread, rusty dun
Shuck: Zelon, caddis color, half the length of the body
Body: 4–6 pheasant tail barbs
Ribbing: Thread
Wing: Zelon, cream or dun
Thorax: Hareline Hare’s Ear Dub

snippet.title: Pheasant Tail X Caddis by Craig Mathews | Fly Recipe
snippet.description:
Caddis, like mayflies, can experience difficulties escaping their pupal shucks. Many end up
trapped with their shucks trailing off their wings, bodies or legs. Big, selective trout will usually refuse to take high-floating patterns like elk hair caddis, instead feeding on impaired adults like the X-caddis. Using pheasant tail fibers for the body of the adults with a trailing shuck of Zelon and deer- or elk-hair wings is a deadly combination.

MATERIALS
Hook: Tiemco TMC 100BL or similar hook, #14–#20
Thread: 8/0 UNI-Thread to match body color
Shuck: Zelon, caddis color
Body: 4–8 pheasant tail barbs
Ribbing: Thread
Thorax: Olive, amber or tan Zelon Dubbing Blend
Wing: Deer hair
Head: Trimmed butts of deer-hair wing

snippet.title: Pheasant Tail Zelon Midge by Craig Mathews | Fly Recipe
snippet.description:
The pheasant tail Zelon midge imitates an emerging midge trapped in its pupal shuck. Trout feed eagerly on these helpless emergers since they know these insects can’t escape the water’s surface. During heavy midge hatches when big fish are taking drifting pupae, this fly often outperforms standard pupal patterns.

MATERIALS
Hook: Tiemco TMC 2488 or 100BL, #18–#26
Thread: 8/0 UNI-Thread to match body color (olive dun or black is the most common)
Shuck: Zelon or Para Post, medium or dark dun, or none
Body: The shuck, ribbed
Wings: Zelon or Para Post, medium or dark dun
Thorax: 2–3 black natural pheasant tail barbs

snippet.title: Pheasant Tail Simplicity | Full Trailer
snippet.description:
In their new book, Pheasant Tail Simplicity, three legendary anglers — Yvon Chouinard,  Craig Mathews, and Mauro Mazzo — make the case that, when it comes to fooling trout, less is more. Published by Patagonia Books, the guide features step-by-step instructions for 18 essential fly patterns, all tied using feathers from a single source: the tail of a male ring-necked pheasant. QR codes throughout the book link to instructional videos demonstrating tying techniques and fishing methods that catch fish from Montana trout streams to Patagonian rivers to Caribbean bonefish flats.

Buy the book here: https://pat.ag/YT/PheasantTail

snippet.title: Lor Sabourin | Green Mojave (5.13) | Microbeta #4 | Patagonia
snippet.description:
Some of the climbs that stick with you are the ones that have it all, and according to Patagonia Climb Ambassador Lor Sabourin, The Green Mojave (5.13) in northern Arizona is one of them. In episode 4 of our short film series “Microbeta,” Lor describes some of the mental tactics they used to figure out how to send this intricate corner crack.  

Microbeta is all about the details. It’s the sneaky weight shift, the precise finger position or the subtle mental unlock that takes a project from “impossible” to “doable.” And it’s our celebration of the weird, obsessive specificity of rock climbing. Our new short film series, “Microbeta,” takes you into the minutiae of our ambassadors' processes, celebrating the unique creativity they bring to their trickiest and most meaningful ascents. 

Watch the series here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLJQsrK_W2jnjCy9OjypH61zLgHVUoR1Jc

snippet.title: Seeking South
snippet.description:
Seeking South follows trail runner Keisuke Minami as he takes on the fastest-known-time (FKT) challenge of the Grand Randonée 10 (GR10)—a grueling 914 km journey across the Pyrenees in southern France, from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. The route typically takes 45-60 days to complete, but Minami sets out to finish in just over 9 days.

Why would someone willingly endure pain, isolation, and total exhaustion? What might keep him running? Minami, whose name means "south" in Japanese, runs across the mountains as the film pursues the story behind his relentless drive.

A story of obsession, resilience, and the demons that push us forward, Seeking South is an intimate look at the mind of an endurance athlete and the weight of the past he runs to escape—or embrace.

snippet.title: The Runner's Cut of Pocatello Round
snippet.description:
In the summer of 2024, Luke Nelson set out to run the visual skyline of his hometown Pocatello, Idaho: an estimated 60 miles and 20,000 feet of vert. It was a run he’d been dreaming of for two decades. Four times, he’d tried and failed. The fifth, he decided to ask for help. As it turned out, community made all the difference. This is the story of that day, through Luke's eyes.

"As we worked on telling the story of the Pocatello Round, I found myself really wanting to dive deeper into the heart of the experience — not mine personally, but the shared experience of a whole community that came out to support me. The result is a 'runner's cut' of the film. It includes more about my pacers, crew and friends, and explores the influence these people can have on our lives. I hope it gives everyone a deeper appreciation for your own communities and the people in your life who make big ideas possible." - Luke Nelson

snippet.title: Aloha: Repair is An Act of Love | Patagonia Stories
snippet.description:
“She has the structure, I have the dreams. And when we connect, there’s magic.” The relationship between Sabrina and Vanessa is almost symbiotic—a powerful and close-knit bond they build day by day among waves, the beach, and the machines in their workshop, Aloha Surf. Together, they’ve brought more than 3,000 wetsuits back to life—and in doing so, kept over 50 tons of material from turning into waste.

Discover the story of “Alohas”—a tale of love, courage, perseverance, and triumph, where what many see as trash gave them the chance to dream of a happy ending.

“Ella tiene una estructura, yo tengo los sueños. Y cuando las dos nos conectamos, hay magia”, La relación de Sabrina y Vanessa es casi simbiótica, un vínculo poderoso y cómplice que construyen día a día entre olas, playa y las máquinas de su taller, Aloha Surf, con las que ya han devuelto la vida a más de 3.000 trajes de surf —y de paso evitado que más de 50 toneladas de material se conviertan en basura.

Conoce la historia de  “las Aloha”, una historia de amor, arrojo, perseverancia y victorias, en la que eso que muchos consideran desecho les permitió soñar con un final feliz.

snippet.title: Worn Wear | Stories We Wear: Spencer Siefke
snippet.description:
Meet Spencer in a new episode of "The Stories We Wear," Worn Wear’s video series about great tales of gear as told by their humans. 

Snap-T® fleeces, Better Sweater® jackets and Mongolian battle armor circa 18th century are just a few of the many items repair pro Spencer Siefke sources from landfills around the world, including from Moldova, Pakistan and the Philippines. Instead of letting perfectly functional, great quality gems create more trash our planet doesn’t need, Spencer hand-fixes each garment and sells them through his platform Wabi Wear Repair. 

Explore quality used Patagonia gear on WornWear.com .

Featuring Spencer and Jeneen Siefke

snippet.title: Sea Country | Patagonia Films
snippet.description:
Sea Country — Malu Lag follows Tishiko King — a marine biologist and proud Kulkalaig woman — all the way to the United Nations Climate Change Conference in Dubai. It’s a long way from her island home of Masig, but she makes the trip to try and save it.

Malu Lag explores the great healing power of the ocean, the resolve of a First Nations community to protect their island and culture, and one woman’s journey to stand up for the place she loves.

snippet.title: Uplifted Book (Trailer) | Patagonia Books
snippet.description:
Explore Uplifted: The Evolution of a Climbing Life (by Sonnie Trotter): https://www.patagonia.com/product/uplifted-the-evolution-of-a-climbers-life/BK930.html/BK930.html?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organicvideo&utm_campaign=yt_s25_BK930
When Sonnie Trotter first tried climbing at age  15, he knew he’d found the path he was meant to follow. Now, thirty years later, he’s looking back on a life spent pushing himself and the sport, chasing adventures in wild places. His new memoir, “Uplifted,” includes stories that span his climbing career, including his legendary first free ascent of the 5.14 trad testpiece Cobra Crack, climbs with friends Tommy Caldwell, Chris Sharma and Alex Honnold, and reflections on risk as a husband and father. One of the strongest and most positive climbers of our time, Sonnie manages to hold even his gnarliest experiences lightly and his writing offers hard-earned wisdom with the personal and friendly delivery of tales told around the campfire.
